title: Terraform networking patterns: subnet topology, egress NAT/IGW, VPC endpoints, and endpoint health guardrails
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and companion docs that capture Redwood's preferred VPC networking patterns for private deployments. The module must support configurable subnet topologies (single-AZ, multi-AZ, per-AZ private/public subnets), pluggable egress patterns (managed NAT Gateway per AZ, centralized NAT/egress instance, or IGW-only for public workloads), first-class VPC endpoint configuration (S3, DynamoDB, CloudWatch Logs, Systems Manager, ECR where applicable), route table composition, and automated health detection + remediation guidance for critical network components. Deliverables include code, integration tests, upgrade/migration guidance for existing private customers, and runbook examples for on-call/ops teams.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a clear public interface (inputs/outputs) for subnet counts, AZ distribution, and egress mode; examples for at least AWS and a note for Azure/GCP mapping.
Supports three egress modes: per-AZ managed NAT Gateway, centralized NAT (single egress with HA recommendation), and IGW-only. Cost/availability trade-offs documented.
VPC endpoint resources are optional but declarable via a map; module creates endpoint policies and route table associations where required.

Automated healthcheck hooks: CloudWatch alarms for NAT gateway error metrics and endpoint reachability; sample Lambda remediation playbook and a canary test (small EC2 or container) to validate egress and endpoint access.
Outputs include subnet ids grouped by role, main route table id, egress resource ids, and recommended tags for RBAC/audit.
Module passes Terraform unit tests (terratest) and a CI integration run in our staging account; PR includes test results and a deployment example.
Migration guide explains step-by-step for migrating existing VPCs to module-managed resources with minimal downtime; includes rollback instructions.
Security review completed and findings addressed (KMS references, endpoint policies least privilege).
tasks: Draft interface and example usage (inputs/outputs, defaults) - 2 days
Implement multi-AZ subnet and route table resource set - 3 days
Implement egress modes and toggle logic, add tagging and IAM roles - 2 days
Add VPC endpoint map support with policy generation - 2 days
Add CloudWatch alarms + sample Lambda remediation + canary test - 3 days
Write docs, migration guide, and runbooks; update console onboarding steps - 2 days
Create CI pipeline tests (terratest) and run in staging - 2 days
Open PR, address code review feedback, and merge - 1-2 days
discussion: Trade-off: per-AZ managed NAT Gateways are simple/HA but cost 2-3x vs centralized NAT. Decision: support both; default to per-AZ for production, centralized as opt-in for cost-sensitive non-critical workloads.
Design note: prefer route table composition over inlining routes so rollouts can swap route associations with minimal changes.

Healthchecks: we evaluated Route53 health checks vs CloudWatch synthetic canary. Chosen approach: CloudWatch alarms + small periodic canary (Fargate task) to verify egress and endpoints and surface to Console/Incidents.

Compatibility: module will maintain compatibility with existing terraform state by using importable resource naming patterns and aliasing where needed; migration guide will show terraform state mv/import commands.
Security feedback from SRE: endpoint policies must be generated with least privilege and bind to IAM role ARNs rather than broad principals; added as mandatory validation in CI linting.
PM feedback: provide clear cost estimator examples in docs showing monthly cost delta between egress modes for 3 common workload profiles.
